config.title: Test User Interactions

intro.title: Test User Interactions
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component with a button and test how a user can interact with it. You will learn the core concept of simulating user events, like clicks, to verify that your component responds correctly. The main technologies involved are Angular's Component Testing utilities and the Jasmine testing framework. By the end, you'll be able to write a test that clicks a button and checks if the expected action occurs.
intro.usecase: Testing user interactions is essential for ensuring that interactive UI components behave correctly in real-world applications. For example, in e-commerce checkout forms, developers must verify that quantity selectors update totals, promo code inputs apply discounts, and payment buttons trigger the correct submission flow. Similarly, in dashboard applications, interaction tests validate that filter controls update data visualizations, tab switches display appropriate content, and modal dialogs open/close as expected. These tests prevent user-facing bugs in critical workflows where incorrect behavior could lead to lost sales, data errors, or poor user experience.

objectives: Initialize a test component with user interaction elements
Configure test utilities to simulate user events
Implement event handlers for user interactions in test scenarios
Apply assertions to verify user interaction outcomes
Manipulate component state through simulated user actions
Integrate user interaction tests within a test suite
Render components and trigger user events in test environments

steps.title: Import Component, CommonModule, and FormsModule
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core', CommonModule from '@angular/common', and FormsModule from '@angular/forms' at the top of your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbol name and the module path. Separate multiple imports with commas.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component, CommonModule, and FormsModule here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules and decorator are imported for building and testing user interaction components.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core', CommonModule from '@angular/common', and FormsModule from '@angular/forms'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but not all required ones. Make sure to import Component from '@angular/core', CommonModule from '@angular/common', AND FormsModule from '@angular/forms'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Component from '@angular/core', CommonModule from '@angular/common', and FormsModule from '@angular/forms' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main component class
steps.instruction:
Create a component class named InteractionTestComponent with the @Component decorator. Include the selector 'app-interaction-test' and template '

Interaction test component

'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component. Remember to export the class.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic Angular component class ready for adding interactive features in later steps.
successCriteria: InteractionTestComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, proper selector, and template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have: 1) @Component decorator with selector and template, 2) exported class named InteractionTestComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you're using the @Component decorator and exporting the class.

steps.title: Initialize component state properties
steps.instruction: Inside the InteractionTestComponent class, add three typed properties: clickCount (number) initialized to 0, inputText (string) initialized to an empty string, and isActive (boolean) initialized to false.
steps.hint: Define these properties directly in the class body with type annotations and initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class will have three typed state properties with initial values ready for user interaction testing.
successCriteria: The InteractionTestComponent class contains clickCount: number = 0, inputText: string = '', and isActive: boolean = false properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some properties, but make sure all three are present with correct types and initial values: clickCount (number=0), inputText (string=''), and isActive (boolean=false).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't have the required typed properties. Add clickCount: number = 0, inputText: string = '', and isActive: boolean = false inside the class.

steps.title: Define input change handler
steps.instruction: Add a method named updateText that takes an event parameter and updates the inputText property with the event target's value.
steps.hint: Define a method in the component class that receives an event parameter. Access the value from event.target.value and assign it to this.inputText.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can handle text input changes by updating the inputText property.
successCriteria: The updateText method is defined in the component class, takes an event parameter, and assigns event.target.value to this.inputText.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your method takes an event parameter and updates this.inputText with the value from event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateText method is not properly defined. Check that it's in the component class, takes an event parameter, and updates this.inputText.

steps.title: Define toggle handler method
steps.instruction: Add a toggleActive() method to your component class that flips the value of the isActive property.
steps.hint: Create a method that toggles the boolean value using the logical NOT operator (!).
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a toggleActive() method that can be called to reverse the isActive state.
successCriteria: toggleActive() method is defined and correctly toggles the isActive property using the logical NOT operator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check if it properly toggles the isActive property using the ! operator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleActive() method is missing or doesn't correctly toggle the isActive property. Remember to use the logical NOT operator (!) to flip the boolean value.

steps.title: Add component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template section with a main container div and appropriate Angular template syntax
steps.hint: Add a template property to the @Component decorator that contains a <div> element with a class or id attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic template structure with a container div ready for UI elements.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a template property with a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a template, but make sure it contains a <div> element with proper Angular syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is missing or incorrect. Add a template property with a <div> element inside the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Add click interaction button
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add a button element with a (click) event binding that calls the incrementClick() method. Also add a paragraph element that displays the current clickCount value.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="incrementClick()" on the button. For the paragraph, use interpolation with double curly braces to show the clickCount property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button that increments clickCount when clicked and a paragraph that displays the current clickCount value.
successCriteria: The template contains a button with (click)="incrementClick()" and a paragraph with {{ clickCount }} interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the button with the (click) event binding and the paragraph showing {{ clickCount }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet contain the required button and paragraph. Remember to use Angular's event binding syntax and interpolation.

steps.title: Add text input interaction
steps.instruction: Add an input field with two-way data binding to the template using [(ngModel)] bound to the inputText property, and display the current value in a paragraph below.
steps.hint: Use the ngModel directive with banana-in-a-box syntax [(ngModel)] to bind the input field to the inputText property. Then add a paragraph that shows the current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include an input field that updates the inputText property in real-time, and a paragraph that displays the current input value.
successCriteria: The template contains an input field with [(ngModel)]="inputText" and a paragraph that displays {{ inputText }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the input field with [(ngModel)] and a paragraph showing {{ inputText }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field or paragraph is missing or not properly bound. Check that you're using [(ngModel)] and displaying the value correctly.

steps.title: Add toggle interaction button
steps.instruction: Add a button below the existing input field that toggles the isActive state when clicked and displays conditional text based on that state.
steps.hint: Use (click) to call toggleActive() and use *ngIf or a ternary to show different text based on isActive.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggle button that changes isActive state and shows different UI text based on that state.
successCriteria: Button with (click)="toggleActive()" exists and displays conditional text using isActive state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check if it properly calls toggleActive() and shows conditional text based on isActive.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle button or its conditional display is missing or incorrect.
